chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Kamil al-Tammar, who said:
Do you know who they are? I said: You know better.
He said: Certainly, the believers who have succeeded are the submitters. Indeed, the submitters are the noble chosen ones. So the believer is a stranger; therefore, glad tidings for the strangers.

key_terms.النُّجَبَاءُ: the noble and select ones; people of distinction and excellence
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: the believers; those characterized by true faith and spiritual success
key_terms.الْمُسَلِّمُونَ: the submitters; those who enter into submission to Allah
key_terms.طُوبَى: glad tidings, blessedness, and goodness reserved for the righteous
key_terms.غَرِيبٌ: a stranger; one whose true faith makes him uncommon among people

ai.seo_question: Who are the successful believers, and why is the true believer described as a stranger?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an explanation of the Quranic declaration that the believers are successful. Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) distinguishes between outward submission and the deeper station of faith, describing the true believer as a stranger among people. It highlights the rarity and special merit of genuine iman and gives glad tidings to those who remain steadfast despite estrangement.
